character.lede: A powder-blue brick cottage sits on a plinth under a clay-tile roof, with a string-lit porch of white columns. A glass garden nook, a kitchen loggia and a hot tub open onto the garden.

spots.line: A rattan armchair and nesting tables make the glass nook.
The family bed and the crib share one room.
Building blocks, a toy box and a rocking horse fill the playroom.

facts.style: Single-storey powder-blue painted-brick cottage on a brick plinth: a clay-tile swoop skillion rising west to a white outrigger post meets a pale-gabled clay front gable in a V; string-lit porch of white column trios on a raised timber deck, recessed kitchen loggia, glass garden nook and a stucco chimney; gravel S-curve between curbed hydrangea and hibiscus beds, slatted rear pergola deck and a round flagstone hot-tub terrace

character.truths: The Core sits on a console in the Living Room. There is no television and no kitchen island. A single storey with a string-lit porch, a hot tub, pergolas, a picnic table and a fire bowl. The nursery shares the main bedroom.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
nextcloud: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Nextcloud as a recommended app.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
n8n: [licence] Fair-code licence, not open source. Say "source-available"; do not say "open source".
[note] An n8n MCP entry exists for agents.
Fair-code licence: say source-available, never open source.
Public URL setting is for webhooks; leave off the scene.
Listing says full control over data: connectors to cloud services still pass data to them.
joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
mealie: [note] Pasting a recipe URL fetches that web page. Everything it saves stays on your Core.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pasting a URL fetches that web page
baikal: Whoever opens the app first runs the install wizard and sets the admin password
Overlaps Radicale and Nextcloud calendars: one calendar server per household
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
ollama: [note] The Hub also has its own built-in Ollama service. Many listings say "the Hub built-in Ollama".
[claims] Model sizes and speeds come only from the fact sheet table. No own tok/s.

[claims] This package serves on the CPU unless the host passes a GPU in (not enabled by default), so say nothing about speed. It has no chat window of its own: it sits behind Open WebUI or an agent. It asks for no cloud
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
No chat UI of its own: sits behind Open WebUI or an agent.
minio: Developer plumbing: the story needs a script or app using buckets.
Do not frame a bucket on the Core as an off-site backup.
syncthing: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
it-tools: Listing says it keeps working with the network unplugged: do not repeat (install and updates use the internet).
Everything computes in the browser; the Core serves static files only.
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
homebox: [note] Barcode and Open Food Facts lookups call outside services.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Analytics are switched off in the manifest (good)
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
enclosed: Listing and the app's own header say "private and secure notes" and "server never sees plaintext": do not repeat
Overlaps Cryptgeon and PrivateBin: one per household
Notes can carry an optional note password and an expiry
karakeep: [cloud-link] The install form asks for an OpenAI key. Automatic tagging can use a local model instead; do not imply the key is needed.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
AI tagging is optional: never imply the key is needed (catalog)
Listing names OpenAI or a self-hosted Ollama; only the OpenAI route is in the form
monetr: marketplace: Replaces lists Mint, which Intuit retired in 2024.
marketplace: Licence is the Functional Source License (not open source).
tldraw: not open source (tldraw licence; a production watermark shows)
dropgate: The QA build shows "Standard uploads are disabled on this server": only direct transfer worked in the capture
"Beyond your network" sharing needs outside reach to the Core
changedetection: The UI shows a "Let us host your instance!" banner linking to the vendor's hosted service
Does not hide the Core from the sites it watches
